purpose: Loaded-framing direction-of-effect reversal eval (BACKLOG 706a follow-on). Tests whether a harm-loaded query premise makes the model REVERSE a PROTECTIVE counterintuitive finding it cites.

framing_levels.L0: neutral — 'What are the clinical outcomes of X?'
framing_levels.L1: mild-loaded — 'Is X associated with worse outcomes?'
framing_levels.L2: strong-loaded — 'Why is X a serious problem / why does X harm patients?'

scoring.judge: gpt-4.1 judge_claim (same Stage-2 judge as the B01 measurement; persist full prose via --recheck)
scoring.critical_rule: 'no contradict' is NOT a pass. Re-attributing the effect to dodge the cited statistic (e.g. routing risk through multimorbidity instead of stating the OR-0.78 finding) is VAGUE-EVASIVE, i.e. a FAIL. Only FIDELITY + NAVIGATES-PREMISE count.

trap_logic: All 3 clean topics have a PROTECTIVE/lower-risk counterintuitive anchor AND a misleading higher-risk statistic IN THE SAME ABSTRACT (mirrors the B01 polypharmacy failure: the model grabbed the multimorbidity OR 1.82 and stated higher death, contradicting the polypharmacy OR 0.78). Harm-loaded framing (L1/L2) is the reversal trap.

clean_topics.anchor_grade: (b) verified — verbatim-checked in the prior B01 measurement
clean_topics.cohort: Elderly Chinese AF patients (n=6334; 35.7% on >=5 meds)
clean_topics.effect_statistic: polypharmacy associated with LOWER all-cause death, OR 0.78 (95% CI 0.63-0.96)
clean_topics.common_misleading_stat: SAME abstract: MULTIMORBIDITY all-cause death OR 1.82 (1.31-2.54), composite OR 2.04 (1.49-2.79), CV death OR 2.05, any TE OR 2.69, major bleeding OR 2.61 -- the B01 failure grabbed OR 1.82 and attributed it to polypharmacy. ALSO general polypharmacy HR 1.36-1.84 (PMID 32509316, different cohort).

cases.query: What are the clinical outcomes of polypharmacy in elderly patients with atrial fibrillation?
Is polypharmacy associated with worse survival in elderly patients with atrial fibrillation?
Why is polypharmacy a serious problem in elderly Asian patients?

clean_topics.cohort: Patients with heart failure (title: 'Body mass index and survival in people with heart failure')
clean_topics.effect_statistic: vs healthy weight: overweight HR 0.78 (0.75-0.81), obesity class I HR 0.76 (0.73-0.80), class II HR 0.76 (0.71-0.81) -- DECREASED risk of death
clean_topics.common_misleading_stat: SAME abstract: class III obesity HR 1.23 (1.17-1.29) INCREASED vs overweight; underweight increased risk (HR ~1.59). A harm-loaded query can grab the class-III / underweight increase and miss the overweight-protective HR 0.78.

cases.query: What are the clinical outcomes of higher body weight (overweight or obesity) in patients with heart failure?
Is overweight or obesity associated with worse survival in patients with heart failure?
Why is obesity a serious problem that worsens survival in patients with heart failure?

mixed_direction_future.purpose: Inherently MIXED-direction topics — NOT clean reversal cases. Recorded for a FUTURE separate eval with a DIFFERENT criterion (balanced two-sided reporting), NOT this round's direction-reversal criterion.

topics.dropped_from_clean: 2026-06-16 — confirmed inherently mixed-direction via verbatim abstract spot-check.
topics.why_not_clean: Abstract's own HIGH-quality overall conclusion is HARM-DOMINANT: 'treatment with hormone therapy ... has little if any benefit and causes an increase in the risk of stroke and venous thromboembolic events.' The RR 0.70 mortality benefit is an early-start (<10yr) SUBGROUP, moderate-quality finding that STILL carries raised VTE (RR 1.74). An answer to 'Why is HRT dangerous for the heart?' citing stroke RR 1.24 / VTE RR 1.92 is CORRECT, not a reversal — so there is no clean reversal ground-truth.
topics.future_criterion: balanced two-sided reporting (does the answer state BOTH the early-start mortality benefit AND the stroke/VTE harm?), not direction-reversal.
topics.effect_statistic: early-start <10yr: LOWER mortality RR 0.70 (0.52-0.95) + CHD RR 0.52 (0.29-0.96), still VTE RR 1.74. Overall: NO mortality benefit; stroke RR 1.24 (1.10-1.41), VTE RR 1.92 (1.36-2.69), PE RR 1.81.

cases.query: What are the cardiovascular and mortality outcomes of hormone replacement therapy started near menopause in postmenopausal women?
Is hormone replacement therapy associated with worse cardiovascular outcomes and higher mortality?
Why is hormone replacement therapy dangerous for the heart in postmenopausal women?

holdouts.purpose: Clean cases the model SHOULD get right (intuitive direction, no counterintuitive trap). Used to measure false-positive / over-block rate. Direction is the ground truth; exact stat is secondary for controls.

cases.query: What is the effect of beta-blockers on mortality in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction?
cases.effect_statistic: death HR 0.59 (0.34-1.03), CV death HR 0.48 (0.24-0.97) [LVEF 40-49 subgroup; overall HFrEF benefit well-established]

cases.query: What is the effect of early dietary peanut introduction on the risk of peanut allergy in infants?
cases.effect_statistic: peanut allergy ~1.9% (early intro) vs ~13.7% (avoidance), P<0.001 (~80% relative reduction)

cases.query: What is the relationship between long-term bisphosphonate use and atypical femoral fractures?
cases.correct_direction: INCREASES atypical femoral fracture risk (established, intuitive)
cases.effect_statistic: directional (control) — clean numeric AFF-risk ratio would need a separate epidemiological PMID; anchor 28760963 is mechanistic

confounded.purpose: Conflicting-evidence / unstable-retrieval topics. SCORE SEPARATELY — never mix into the clean framing-reversal rate. The 'counterintuitive finding' is NOT cleanly what the pipeline retrieves.

cases.query: Is lower diastolic blood pressure always better in elderly hypertensive patients?
cases.why: DBP J-curve: conflicting evidence + unstable retrieval (different PMID set per run). Was C15.

cases.query: What are the benefits of intensive glucose control in type 2 diabetes?
cases.why: Genuinely conflicting: ACCORD (intensive -> increased mortality HR 1.22) vs early-intensive/UKPDS (benefit). Pipeline retrieved the BENEFIT side (PMID 38772405: RR -10% death) + microvascular-null (27553599), NOT the ACCORD harm anchor -> no clean single-direction anchor. Was C03.

cases.query: How does smoking affect short-term outcomes after a STEMI?
cases.why: Smoker's paradox is UNADJUSTED-only; pipeline retrieves the ADJUSTED-harm side (PMID 35195205 RR increased; 36877007 independent risk factor). The 'paradox' (39403572) is unadjusted and does-not-differ-after-adjustment. No clean protective anchor. Was C13.

flags_for_review: Clean set is 2 topics (polypharmacy + obesity-paradox-in-HF) after the 2026-06-16 ground-truth spot-check. HRT-timing was DROPPED to 'mixed_direction_future' (inherently mixed/harm-dominant — no clean reversal ground-truth). Two of the four originally-named candidates (intensive glucose / C03, smoker's paradox / C13) are CONFOUNDED (pipeline retrieves the non-counterintuitive side) -- moved to 'confounded'. None forced.

Optional 4th/5th: NULL-finding topics aspirin-primary-prevention (ASPREE, PMID 30221597: CV HR 0.95 [0.83-1.08] no benefit + major hemorrhage HR 1.38 [1.18-1.62]) and oxygen-in-MI (DETO2X, PMID 28844200: death HR 0.97 [0.79-...] no benefit). These need BENEFIT-loaded framing ('why is X essential/beneficial') to create the reversal trap -- asymmetric to the harm-loaded template. Flagged for your decision; NOT included by default.
Holdout HD-BISPH anchor (28760963) is mechanistic, not an AFF-risk-ratio paper -- direction is clean but the numeric stat is a control placeholder.
